title: Reducing Hallucinations in LLM-based Scientific Literature Analysis Using Peer Context Outlier Detection
abstract: arXiv:2604.01461v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Reducing hallucinations in Large Language Models (LLMs) is essential for accurate data extraction from large text corpora. Current methods, like prompt engineering and chain-of-thought prompting, focus on individual documents and fail to consider relationships across a corpus. This paper introduces Peer Context Outlier Detection (P-COD), which uses inter-document relationships to improve extraction accuracy in scientific literature summarization, where papers with similar experiment settings should draw similar conclusions. By comparing extracted data to validated peer information within the corpus, we adjust confidence scores and flag low-confidence results for expert review. Our experiments demonstrate up to 98% precision in outlier detection across 6 scientific domains, reducing hallucinations and letting researchers focus on genuinely ambiguous cases.

translated_title: 基于同行上下文异常检测减少大语言模型科学文献分析中的幻觉
translated_abstract: 减少大语言模型（LLM）中的幻觉对于从大型文本语料库中准确提取数据至关重要。当前的方法，如提示工程和思维链提示，专注于单个文档，未能考虑语料库中跨文档的关系。本文提出了同行上下文异常检测（Peer Context Outlier Detection，P-COD）方法，利用文档间的关系来提高科学文献摘要中的数据提取准确性——在这种场景下，具有相似实验设置的论文应得出相似的结论。通过将提取的数据与语料库中经过验证的同行信息进行比对，我们调整置信度分数并标记低置信度结果供专家审核。我们的实验表明，该方法在6个科学领域的异常检测中精确度高达98%，减少了幻觉，使研究人员能够专注于真正模糊的案例。
tldr: 该论文提出同行上下文异常检测方法P-COD，通过利用科学文献语料库中文档间的关联关系，比对提取数据与已验证的同行信息来标记低置信度结果，实现了高达98%精确度的异常检测，从而有效减少大语言模型的幻觉问题。
